parameters.content:
## Block merge requests that break EU Accessibility Act basics

Since 28 June 2025 the European Accessibility Act covers online shops, banking and ticketing sold in the EU. This workflow puts an accessibility check into every GitLab merge request.

### How it works
1. GitLab reports each opened or updated merge request.
2. The changed web files are read at the merge request's own commit. Only the lines it adds can block; problems already on the target branch are counted, never blamed.
3. Fixed rules check what markup can prove: image alt text, form labels, page language, empty buttons and links, frame titles, inline colour contrast, tabindex and autoplay. Each finding names its WCAG 2.1 criterion.
4. A commit status passes or fails, and one comment lists every problem with its fix. The comment is edited on every push, never repeated.
5. A file that cannot be read fails the check. The waiver label passes it on purpose.

### Setup
1. Connect GitLab, and type the group and project in the trigger.
2. Activate the workflow, so the trigger registers its webhook.
3. To block merging, turn on "Pipelines must succeed" in the project's merge request settings.

### Good to know
This reads source, not the rendered page. It is a floor for code review, not an audit.

## 1. A merge request changes
All settings live in Accessibility Rules.

## 2. Which lines did it add?
Only web files, and only added lines can block.

## 3. Check what markup can prove
Each finding names its WCAG 2.1 criterion and the fix.

## 4. Pass or block
A file that cannot be read blocks. The waiver label passes on purpose.

## 5. One comment, kept up to date
Edited on every push, never repeated.
